entries.644b6564bfeb1e7e: This category is described in the securities report as “business segments not included in reportable segments” and includes 17 consolidated subsidiaries (14 in the prior year). The securities report does not describe the business content of this category individually. In the table of principal facilities, Takara Sangyo Co., Ltd., which holds production facilities at plants in Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture and elsewhere, is included in this category, and the MD&A describes Takara Sangyo as a company that “is responsible for developing and manufacturing ramen ingredients.” The MD&A lists the ramen business as one of the pillars of its medium-term management plan strategy, but does not state how it corresponds to this category. In the fiscal year ended February 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥13,357 million (up 38.7% year on year), segment profit was ¥694 million, and production results were ¥2,618 million (up 73.1% year on year). Because it is not a reportable segment, it is listed last.

entries.9dc403ceb086deec: This business operates “Yoshinoya” fast-food outlets in Japan, selling gyudon and other dishes, and provides management guidance to franchised outlets. The principal company is Yoshinoya Co., Ltd., and the company is carrying out an organizational restructuring to merge six domestic Yoshinoya operating companies into one company, Yoshinoya Co., Ltd. Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended February 2026 was ¥150,190 million (up 9.8% year on year), the largest of the reportable segments. Segment profit (based on operating profit) was ¥7,623 million (down 2.1% year on year), affected by cost increases, mainly for raw materials. The number of stores at the end of the period was 1,290; during the period, 51 stores opened and 20 closed. Stores with the new service models (Cooking & Comfort and Jigsaw Counter) increased by 50 to 590, and 897 stores had tablets installed; the company plans to introduce tablets in all stores during fiscal 2026.

entries.e47308a1375c4627: This business operates self-service Sanuki udon and other fast-food outlets under the “Hanamaru” name in Japan, and provides management guidance to franchised outlets. The principal company is Hanamaru Co., Ltd. (Takamatsu City, Kagawa Prefecture). In the fiscal year ended February 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥32,795 million (up 6.9% year on year) and segment profit was ¥2,427 million (up 21.0% year on year). The number of stores at the end of the period was 418; during the period, 16 stores opened and 13 closed. To advance dominant store openings (concentrating store openings in a specific area) in major metropolitan areas, it opened “Zuzuzu,” a new format compact model store of 20 tsubo, in Nihonbashi, Tokyo, in October 2025. In addition, under the “Oidemai! Sanuki Project,” launched on the occasion of the 25th anniversary of its founding, the noodles at 14 stores in Kagawa Prefecture were switched to noodles made from the Kagawa-grown wheat “Sanuki no Yume.”
